name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+11 partisan lean
Incumbent Brandon Gill running with a large financial advantage ($4.2M raised vs $17K)
Prediction markets price Gill at 97% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: Gill combines a solidly Republican district, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising edge over Democrat Steven Shook, while markets give him a 97% chance. With no polling or ratings suggesting otherwise, the race sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unusually strong Democratic spending surge could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Texas's 26th District is a solidly Republican seat, and first-term incumbent Brandon Gill is running for reelection with every structural advantage. The district leans about eleven points Republican, and Gill has raised over $4.2 million while holding $1.4 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Steven Shook, has raised only about $17,000, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets price Gill's chances at 97 percent. The forecast expects Gill to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
